_notes: Ranges of the ISA instance set. Every batch draws its instances with a Latin hypercube over 'instance',
and pairs each generated instance with 'fleet.draws_per_instance' fleets drawn over 'fleet'.
Edit the ranges here; make_batch.py reads this file for every new batch.
A setting given as [low, high] is drawn; a single number is held fixed (it stays out of the hypercube).
Batch 2 (demand pattern, docs/08 and decisions D29-D38):
period_hours 4, requests_per_hour 1250 fixed = 5000 requests per instance (author, from the 2024 mobility report).
start_hour is fixed: for a static solver with a constant travel-time matrix, shifting all times changes nothing,
so it was a dead axis; 14:00 is a leisure-dominated inter-peak afternoon and keeps arrivals far from midnight.
inbound_share (1 = every trip goes from homes to attractions, 0 = the reverse, 0.5 = both ways) and
concentration (count ** concentration; 1 = the OSM counts as they are) replace uniform demand. concentration never reaches 0.
spatial.central_factor 0 removes the central municipalities (Copenhagen, Frederiksberg; metro and S-train) from the service area.
make_batch.py needs zone_weights.py output (with central_share) for these. Scenario labels a/b/c come from inbound_share.

spatial.trip_decay_km: scale L of the zone-level distance decay (a destination zone is kept with 1/(1+(d/L)^2), d from the origin point to the zone centre); null = off. Choose L with check_weights.py.
max_dtt_s 3600 (20 km at 20 km/h); with zone weights the generator ignores the min/max dtt ring around the origin, so it only rejects long trips.
peak_sd_min [20, 120] because the period is 4 h. Fleet percent [10, 40] is provisional (fleets can be redrawn without regenerating).
Batch 1 used period 2 h, 50-500 requests/h, start_hour [12, 19.5], peak_sd [10, 60], fleet [5, 40] and uniform demand.
